brief:
BRIEF FOR TEAM TS3012, before meeting TS3012d (built only from TS3012a, TS3012b, TS3012c).
Who is who: A=Project Manager; B=User Interface Designer; C=Industrial Designer; D=Marketing Expert.

DECIDED SO FAR
- Target is a TV-only universal remote for young consumers (under forty), priced at about 25 euros against a production cost of about 12.5 euros. It covers everyday TV functions, not complicated settings, which stay on the old remote. [TS3012a: "The production price, twelve and a half Euros, approximately."; TS3012b: "it should do what people usually do with their T_V_s, not not the very complicated settings"]
- Core layout: power at top and central, menu button in the middle, and channel/volume controls at the centre as the most important functions. Programme up/down and volume are the main buttons, with small buttons for extras and advanced settings under a menu. Navigation buttons are triangles. [TS3012b: "the bu the power button should be on top, 'cause it's the first thing you do, turn it on."; TS3012b: "Yeah, in the middle. It's it's usually uh there, but"]
- The remote will have a locator: a beep plus a simple LED flash, with the beep as the main signal. C confirms a sound component already exists, so no extra hardware is needed. [TS3012c: "we are going to implement the beep and the flash thing to recover your remote."; TS3012c: "I think that should just be a simple LED or something."]
- An LCD screen is included, placed at the top of the remote, and the chip will be advanced to support it. The team is heading towards the deluxe edition. [TS3012c: "we should take it take it t to consideration to build an L_C_D_ screen in it."; TS3012c: "So we have our L_C_D_ screen. Let's see. In"]
- Speech recognition is now included, because it adds functionality a scroll-wheel lacks. The component is reported to be small enough to fit. The scroll-wheel is out, and push-buttons are used. [TS3012c: "I don't think a scroll-wheel offers new functionality, whereas speech recognition and L_C_D_ screen do offer new functionality in your product."; TS3012c: "Well, the email said it was a quite a small component. So I don't see that."]
- Body: rubber case for a spongy feel, curved so it hangs over the hand, with softened edges, and yellow. Batteries are regular, placed in the lower section. [TS3012c: "I think the spongy feel gives us rubber."; TS3012c: "Then it will bounce and you don't drop it so easily."]
- The remote should look distinct from other brands. Interchangeable covers support a fashionable look, but the clickable removable cover is not in the basic design and may be added later. [TS3012b: "Yeah I think it should be a little distinct from everything else, because it's either"; TS3012c: "So one of these interchangeable covers apparently which will make it a more fashionable product."]

WHAT CHANGED ALONG THE WAY
- Material: the light-material idea from TS3012a was dropped in TS3012b because an LCD and two batteries make the remote a bit heavier. [TS3012a: "the material it is made of, it should be something light."; TS3012b: "But it has to be a little bit heavier."]
- LCD: it was first dropped as too costly and power-hungry, then a text-only or black-and-white preview was considered. It was reinstated in TS3012b 'if not too expensive' and confirmed in TS3012c because the target group wants it and the component is affordable. [TS3012b: "maybe not an L_C_D_ screen but with a preview, but y I'm not sure if it's even possible."; TS3012b: "if it's not too expensive, we should include it, because it's it's cool."]
- Speech recognition: ruled out in TS3012b as immature, memory-hungry and language-dependent. In TS3012c it was included, after the component proved small and about 70% of people reportedly want it. [TS3012b: "I don't think it should be implemented in a remote control yet uh. What else do we have?"; TS3012c: "I don't think a scroll-wheel offers new functionality, whereas speech recognition and L_C_D_ screen do offer new functionality in your product."]
- Energy: rechargeable batteries with a docking station or wired charging were discussed in TS3012b but raised cost concerns. C favoured kinetic power. TS3012c settled on regular batteries. [TS3012b: "But again, isn't that too expensive? 'Cause that means that we have to implement rechargeable batteries, a docking station"; TS3012c: "My personal uh fav favourite is the kinetic provision because uh I ha"]
- Locator: first a button on the TV, then a TV-mounted box or docking station, and finally a beep plus simple LED in TS3012c. [TS3012b: "the beep is a very simple thing to imple implement, just make a button on your T_V_ and just hit the button"; TS3012b: "Maybe just a slap-on sticker with a button which sends out a small signal."]
- Colour: A first proposed the black company colour, then chose yellow after C and D argued for a trendy look for young people. [TS3012c: "I think we should go with uh with the company colour because what specific info that I got from the project board."; TS3012c: "I think we should th then take it take yellow. Take what you c yellow remote control."]
- Covers: C's language-specific covers for older users were rejected because the target is under forty. [TS3012b: "we can also make uh a cover for every language area. That's fo is uh especially for older people"; TS3012c: "we aim for young consumers, so that's fine."]

OPEN ACTIONS AND OWNERS
- Everyone: sketch or doodle a nice design for the next meeting, which A says will complete the design. [TS3012c: "You doodle a doodle us a nice nice design for for the next meeting, we'll be done."]
- Speaker C (Industrial Designer) and Speaker B (User Interface Designer): work together on the final internal and external design. C still owes cost, material and LCD-fit findings. [TS3012c: "apparently you guys, you should work together on the final design, both on internal and external design."; TS3012b: "I hope if I have information about that, I'm gonna"]
- Speaker D (Marketing Expert): do the market analysis and show the user-preference investigation. He must also submit the cost item on a form, and check the exact voice-recognition figure of about 70%. [TS3012c: "you're gonna do the market market uh analysing I'm supposed to do the little work on the year-end report."; TS3012c: "So I can uh show my uh investigation."]
- Speaker A (Project Manager): is writing the year-end project report and still has to get the meeting minutes posted on the web. [TS3012c: "you're gonna do the market market uh analysing I'm supposed to do the little work on the year-end report."; TS3012b: "the minutes will be on the on the web shortly, so there we go"]
- Speaker B (User Interface Designer): earlier committed to drawing UI ideas for the next meeting. [TS3012b: "Or maybe this is something for the next meeting, I can draw out some ideas."]
- Older open research: whether the remote can open the TV's menu, and how a larger LCD and budget would cost out. [TS3012b: "we need to put some research into that if if we can open the menu, I think it's possible"; TS3012b: "We can look at the possibilities for an uh L_C_D_ and uh I dunno. Yeah."]

STILL OPEN / DISAGREEMENTS
- Colour: Speaker B (User Interface Designer) wants a neutral base colour with colour added later via covers. Speaker C (Industrial Designer) wants a flashy yellow remote, and A decided on yellow. [TS3012c: "it's better to have a neutral base colour than to have a flashy"; TS3012c: "I think we should th then take it take yellow. Take what you c yellow remote control."]
- Keypad: Speaker B (User Interface Designer) says twelve buttons would confuse users used to eleven, while A wants an extra button so nothing looks missing. [TS3012c: "Because it's a little bit confusing to have twelve buttons down there, because you're only accustomed to eleven"]
- Fruit-shaped remote: B objects that it ties the product to a seasonal trend. [TS3012c: "But that's just more a se a seasonal, a trend thing."]
- Cost: C warned that an LCD and speech recognition make the target price almost undoable. A says finance is unknown, so cost does not constrain the design. Actual costs remain unchecked. [TS3012b: "Did they really said it like that? Those two things. Do they realise how much that costs? That's almost undoable."; TS3012c: "I'm not sure if we're if we're gonna get finance anyway"]
- Configuring functions through the TV menu is still doubted by C and needs research to confirm. [TS3012b: "But that's the question, is it? Because it needs to be configured in the television under the menu."]
- Edge and curve limits: two curves may not be feasible (C's information), and smoothing the edges adds cost (B). [TS3012c: "But I think, according to my information, this would be two curves."; TS3012c: "What you can do is smooth the edges indeed. But that will bring extra c expenses."]
